_comment: Which rail each electrolytic on A9 sits on, and what that rail runs at.
The rated voltage is NOT here -- it is read from the parts list at run
time, so a corrected BOM corrects this too.
source: 'schematic' means the net was traced on the Chapter 7 sheet cited
in the note; 'inferred' means it was deduced from the rails present at that
slot and has not been read off a schematic. appliedV: null means the rail
was never traced -- shown as unknown rather than assumed safe.
A9's electrolytic population is ten solid tantalums and no aluminium at
all, so there is nothing here whose capacitance can be expected to have
walked with age; what matters on this board is voltage margin. All ten are
traced on the sheets.
railClass is how much energy is behind the rail, which decides what a
shorted part does:
S   +/-17 S from A17, arriving on P312 through chokes L7 and L8 with no
fuse on this board, then dropped through R14/R15 into the local
+17/-17 nodes. A17's regulators are the only current limit.
SW  the same +17 S switched by Q5 to feed the two-wire compensation
converter -- the same energy behind it, live only when PB7 is true.
FU  the unregulated side of the floating supply: the T1 secondary after
CR1/CR9 and CR2/CR10, referenced to ACOM. Current-limited by the
transformer and by 47 ohm R43/R44 downstream.
FR  the regulated floating +/-8A rails, clamped by 8.2 V zeners VR1 and
VR2 behind those same 47 ohm resistors -- the softest rails on the
board, and the only ones referenced to ACOM rather than S COM.
D   the 5 V logic and relay-driver rails from A19 and A17, arriving on
P312 through chokes L5 and L6 and referenced to RLH COM / LH COM.
One finding worth carrying forward: C18 is the tightest margin on the
board. It is a 4.7 uF 25 V part sitting on the switched +17 S node, about
68 percent of rating, where its partner C19 on the same node is a 35 V
part at about 49 percent. That is Fluke's choice and not an extraction
error -- both revisions of Table 6-10 give C18 as 25 V (stock 807644,
Sprague 199D475X0025BA1) and Figure 7-9 sheet 3 shows it on Q5's collector
ahead of L2 -- but it is the part to look at first if this converter has a
history.
C22 and C23's applied voltage is the one number here that is derived rather
than read. Their node is the rectified T1 secondary, which the manual never
publishes; it is VR1/VR2's 8.2 V plus the drop across 47 ohm R43/R44, and
it is bounded above by those zeners' own 0.4 W rating. 10 V is the
conservative end of that range and is what is recorded, so the margin shown
understates rather than overstates.

C7.note: P312 pins 3A/3C -> L7 -> R14 -> the local +17 node feeding the 2/5/10 V source and the differential amplifier. Sheet 2 of 4. R14's value is one of this board's source disagreements: 24 ohm in both parts lists, 30 ohm on the sheet -- either way the drop across it under this load is small and the node sits at essentially +17 S.

C9.note: P312 pins 2A/2C -> L8 -> R15 -> the local -17 node. Mirror of C7. Sheet 2 of 4.

C18.net: +17 S switched by Q5 (U6 supply, ahead of L2)
C18.note: On Q5's collector with C52, ahead of L2. Sheet 3 of 4. A 25 V part on a 17 V node -- the tightest voltage margin on this board, and the reservoir that takes the converter's switching current. Dead when the two-wire compensation circuit is off, because PB7 then holds Q6 and Q5 off and +17 S never reaches this node.

C19.net: +17 S switched by Q5, after L2 (U6 +VIN through R25)
C19.note: With C20 on the far side of L2, feeding U6's +VIN through 1 W resistor R25. Sheet 3 of 4. A 35 V part on the same node C18 sits on at 25 V.

C22.net: T1 secondary, positive rectified (CR1 / CR9), ahead of R43
C22.note: Across the positive rectified secondary to ACOM, before R43 and L3. Sheet 3 of 4. The level is derived, not published: VR1 clamps the far side of R43 at 8.2 V, so this node is 8.2 V plus the drop across 47 ohm, bounded above by VR1's 0.4 W rating. 10 V is the conservative end of that range.

C23.net: T1 secondary, negative rectified (CR2 / CR10), ahead of R44
C23.note: Mirror of C22 on the negative side, before R44 and L4. Sheet 3 of 4. Same derivation, from VR2 rather than VR1.

C24.note: Across VR1 at the +8A rail, after R43 and L3. Sheet 3 of 4. This is TP8's node: §5-11 step 1 expects +8.2 V +/-5 % here referenced to TP7 (ACOM), not to S COM.

C25.note: Across VR2 at the -8A rail, after R44 and L4. Sheet 3 of 4. TP9's node, expected at -8.2 V +/-5 % referenced to TP7.

C33.note: P312 pins 10A/10C -> L5 -> +SRLH, decoupled to RLH COM. Sheet 4 of 4. The bulk reservoir for the seven UCN5801 relay drivers, whose per-chip decoupling is the 0.22 uF row C39-C43 and C45. CORRECTED 2026-08 from 5.0 V to 6.4 V: the net was traced correctly but the rail value was taken from the rail's name. +5 RLH runs at +5.975 V +/-425 mV (Table 2-10, A17 TP14), raised above +5 LH on purpose by R13/CR34/CR35 on A17, so 6.40 V is the top of the published band and the figure the rest of the audit uses. 26 % of a 25 V part rather than 20 %.

C36.note: P312 pins 11A/11C -> L6 -> +5LH, decoupled to LH COM. Sheet 4 of 4. The bulk reservoir for the logic side -- U11, U12, U13, U21 and U22 -- and the largest capacitor on the board at 47 uF. CORRECTED 2026-08 from 5.0 V to 5.1 V, which is Table 2-10's nominal for +5 LH at A17's TP11 (A17's U8 is trimmed above 5 V by R13 and CR34/CR35) and the figure every other board in this audit uses for the rail. On a 10 V part that is 51 % rather than 50 % -- either side of the line, this is a Marginal part and the tightest capacitor on A9 after the +/-17 pair. The band's top, +5.4 V, would make it 54 %.
